history.dynasty: Unknown (legendary: Parashurama; worship attested since 9th century CE per archaeological evidence)
history.summary: Hindu temple on the banks of the Kumaradhara river in Subramanya village (Kadaba taluk, previously Sullia taluk), dedicated to Kartikeya worshipped as Subramanya, lord of all serpents. Per the Skanda Purana's Sahyadri Khanda, Subrahmanya came to Kumara Parvatha after defeating Taraka and Shoorapadmasura, washed his Vel in the Kumaradhara, and gave refuge to serpent-king Vasuki (fleeing Garuda) beneath the mountain. Adi Shankaracharya praised 'Bhaje Kukke Lingam' in his Subrahmanya Bhujangaprayata Stotram; priests are Shivalli Madhwa Brahmins following Madhvacharya's Tantra Sara Sangraha. One of Karnataka's seven Mukti Sthalas; world-famous for Sarpa Samskara, Ashlesha Bali and Naga Prathishta dosha-removal rituals. Coordinates from the official Karnataka HRCE listing (12.663725, 75.615922) corroborate geocoding.

name: Kukke Sri Subrahmanya Temple
town_description: Subramanya (Kukke Subramanya) is a pilgrimage village in Sullia/Kadaba taluk of Dakshina Kannada district, Karnataka, on the banks of the Kumaradhara river. Set in the forested Western Ghats at the foot of Kumara Parvatha, it is renowned for the Kukke Sri Subrahmanya Temple, the foremost centre of Naga worship and Sarpa Samskara rituals in South India. It is also the base for the popular Kumara Parvatha trek.

travel.road: Well connected by road from Mangalore (~105 km) and Bangalore (~270 km); frequent KSRTC buses; Dharmasthala ~54 km away

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (best); Champa Shashti in Margashira is the major festival
